output.brief: FCR fell because of the 14 April Finance change that cut the in-call credit limit from £100 to £25. Larger adjustments are now blocked and automatically referred to the Billing Resolution team. Billing calls referred went from 7% to 54% that same week. Referred calls resolve at about 33%, and non-referred calls still resolve at 82%. Referral rates and the FCR fall are the same across tenure bands: 56% for the April intake, 54% and 53% for the others. So the new starters are not the cause. The tariff mix barely moved, since tariff-call FCR held at 85%. I'm quite sure of this, though I did not check the IVR or workload data directly. Don't put the April intake on performance plans, because that would punish the wrong group. Next step: agree a revised credit limit with Finance, backed by post-call sampling, and trial it on two teams for six weeks. Track FCR and the unsupported-credit rate. Finance has said it would consider this approach. MI can produce the team-level figures within a day. Rebuilding the dashboard is optional and slow.
